summary: Scion was a discontinued Toyota marque launched in 2003 to attract younger customers. It sold sports compact cars, often badge-engineered from Toyota's international models, with a simplified "pure price" approach and a single trim per model that buyers could personalize with factory and aftermarket options. The brand soft launched in California in June 2003, went nationwide by February 2004, entered Canada in 2010, and relied on guerrilla and viral marketing aimed at Generation Y.
one_line: Scion was a discontinued Toyota marque launched in 2003 that sold personalizable sports compacts to younger buyers.
key_facts: Scion is a discontinued marque of Toyota that started in 2003.
Scion was designed as an extension of Toyota's efforts to appeal towards younger customers.
The Scion brand primarily featured sports compact vehicles, primarily badge engineered from Toyota's international models.
The Scion brand offered a simplified "pure price" model.
Scion eschewed trim levels in favor of offering a single trim for each vehicle.
Buyers could personalize Scion vehicles with a range of factory and aftermarket options.
The "Scion" name, meaning the descendant of a family or heir, refers both to the brand's cars and their owners.
The brand first soft launched in the United States at selected Toyota dealers in California in June 2003.
Scion expanded nationwide in the United States by February 2004.
To target the generation Y demographic, Scion primarily relied on guerrilla and viral marketing techniques.
